text:
When you open the communications channel, you hear the voices of soldiers reporting to their superiors, and when the image comes into focus, you see a woman wearing the epaulettes of an Admiral.

"Truth is," explains the slightly graying female Admiral $personName:"The previous mission target has been eliminated for unknown reasons, and our current task at hand is an armaments financing project of considerable magnitude - deliver to me, by any means necessary, three mothballed Yoshura-class starships. What do you think?"

You give careful consideration to this unusual mission...

"What is it? Did you change your mind?"

The female Admiral expressed no urgency, and seemed extremely patient about the matter.

"Very good, I look forward to the good news."

The female Admiral seems relieved as she cut the comms.
"Done so soon?" Over the comms, the female Admiral looks at you with surprise in her eyes.

text:
"Let us meet dockside." The female Admiral takes what has to be the smallest of nods as your consent and cuts the comm link.

You alight at the docks, and after a quick security check, meet the female Admiral face to face.

"Well done." Says the middle aged Admiral, as she taps you on the shoulder.

"See that battlecruiser? In half a month, that old thing will be transferred to Enigma 3 for dismantling. Are you interested in taking a look?"

You ascend to the open side decks, where dense turrets are arranged in a rectangular shape near the center axis... This appears to be a modification of the Yoshura, and combined with her rather unique paint job, you realize that you haven't seen similar warships at the docks... You notice a palm-sized holographic projector sitting on a long table in the command room, out of place among surroundings grayish from the lack of power, the machine is still projecting a bust of a man.

"Rather than a vessel for glory, it is more of a crystallization of memories."

The Admiral walking in front of you mumbles inexplicably before snapping her head back, her right prosthetic eye locking onto yours.

"The mission you completed was merely a test, but before we get to the point, let's talk about something else."

---- Through the dark, narrow maintenance ducts, you follow the Admiral out through the starboard airlock, Port A. ----

The glare of the midday sun makes you squint, as a shrill voice rings in your ears: "All of Enigma were witnesses to our love... and neither of us was prepared for separation, but the gender revolution had reached a turning point."At this point, the Admiral suddenly chokes up a little, and lengthens her tones,"---He was always a quiet man. Who would have known that he would be the one to mobilize the workers of the Orbital Dockyard and the lower ranked Sailors, bringing instability to the outer edges of the galaxy."

"At that time, there was an ongoing war, a massive struggle against the Hegemony. At the beginning, aside from general mobilization, the hawks of war were also at work... The two fleets crept slowly along the edges of a meteorite-strewn galaxy like giant beasts, taking days to close in on each other while carefully pointing their most aggressive fronts at each other. Fleet maneuvers on such scales are a spectacle in the sector. Sub-fleets and scouting groups extended as far as three light-years away. On the first day, fighting went well, with battles fought on four battlefields, and the Hegemony's advance force suffering a severe defeat, reducing one of their battleships to near scrap.

On the second day, fighting was accompanied by a military revolt. He led mutineers in an axial jump, quickly disengaging from the battlefield and firing a surge to jam communications before the upper echelons could react. The situation deteriorated rapidly, and the right flank collapsed. At great cost, we were able to escape, leaving the glory of the Valkyries behind, along with fleet superiority. As one of the three commanders of the right flank, I was impeached, and although I was not convicted of the charges, I have been under house arrest ever since, and as you can see, although I can still express my political views, my voice is not heard."
options: 0:vft_continue:You can't help but lean forward, anticipating further development

text:
"After the battle, the 'traitors' didn't do much more than sail away into the galaxy... But the Valkyries never gave up looking for them." The female Admiral paused and said with a complicated expression:

"In fact, a report of a suspected fleet response in near-Earth orbit of a certain star system remained on my personal computer until I retired... That's where he's hiding, and when his superiors find out, treason and the gallows will be the result.

This needed to end, and I didn't want him to die in shame... That's why I looked for you! You're the only captain with the patience and strength to take care of him for me without a word... And when it's done, you can have all the spoils."

"What... Do you think? " The female Admiral's voice was shaky, and a little distant.

text:
Unexpectedly, you receive a comms request form him, and when you answer, you are surprised to find him talking to himself, as if he understood why you had come.

"You're the one she sent, aren't you? This day has come not a moment too soon."

The leader of the wanderers looks at you through drooping eyelids, looking a bit downtrodden, and more like a roadside beggar than a Fleet Admiral.

"Years of journeying through the void have taken their toll on a ship that used to carry the hopes and passions of the revolutionaries. We tried to build our own utopia, but we lost all our fuel money in the New World. The damned Alliance traders manipulated the fragile colonial economy, creating famine and squeezing the people for every last credit."

"By the time I realized that destroying the trade fleet made it impossible for us to gain a foothold in Alliance worlds, it was too late. The fleet sailed outward, always outward. Across the long outer channel of the Atlantean Nebula to the haunts of outlaws, and through the creepy fringes of the world, we've been through fighting, infighting, fraud and separation again and again, right up to this very moment.

Yet she still holds a grudge against us? You seem to know something about the dark side of the Valkyries, and I wouldn't mind telling you more about it before we fight."
options: 0:vft_he_continue:"Didn't both of you once loved each other? How did it come to this?"

text: "Somehow, communications stalled, and both sides quietly asserted their own justice through their actions... On the eve of the big battle, my followers and I stowed our old carbines and electromagnetic rifles in supply crates and carried them to the battleship. We couldn't miss the chance, when the fearsome interstellar powers were under too much pressure to act, to escape the Valkyrie's sphere of influence!  It was the only way..."
options: 0:vft_he_continue:"There is no denying that it was a great struggle."

text:
"We took control of the sub-fleet in a blitz. The revolutionaries boarded the Yoshura prototype without being detected, killed the guards, whose impulse deflector fields were overwhelmed by our firepower. The capture of this battleship was the movement's crowning achievement."

"The outpost was the last target, and as our heavily armed mob ransacked it, we broke away from the organization and became denizens of the silent void. With the bones of the captured battleship, and the secrets we found in the outpost, I built this war machine, and decided to defend the meaning of my life to the end with iron and blood!"

With determination in his eyes, he raised his right hand to cut off the comm link.
options: 0:vft_he_continue:"If I may ask one last question, what do you think of her now?"

text: "No matter how time passes, she is the only one for me." There is silence on both sides. For a moment, he looks at you, the stars in his eyes seemingly eternal, before resolutely disconnecting the comm link and ending his message abruptly, signaling the end of a story and the coming of a battle.
"I loath her." The comms fall silent, and the flagship shakes violently. You look over the bridge, where someone is shouting "We are under attack! We are under attack!"
"From the moment we abandoned the organization, we had nothing more to do with each other." There comes a buzz, and the comms falls dead.
